headline: SpaceX's Crew-13 launches four astronauts to ISS, sets fastest U.S. docking time on record

supports: On October 1, 2026, SpaceX launched the Crew-13 mission to the International Space Station aboard a Falcon 9 rocket and Crew Dragon spacecraft from Cape Canaveral Space Force Station, Florida, carrying a four-person crew: NASA's Jessica Watkins (commander) and Luke Delaney (pilot), CSA's Joshua Kutryk, and Roscosmos's Sergey Teteryatnikov.
The Crew Dragon docked to the ISS approximately 7 hours 50 minutes after launch, the fastest launch-to-docking time achieved by a U.S. spacecraft in ISS history.

caption:
🇺🇸 SpaceX launched NASA's Crew-13 mission on October 1, bringing four astronauts to the International Space Station aboard a Falcon 9 and Crew Dragon from Cape Canaveral, Florida. The crew — NASA's Jessica Watkins and Luke Delaney, Canada's Joshua Kutryk, and Russia's Sergey Teteryatnikov — docked about 7 hours 50 minutes after liftoff, the fastest launch-to-docking time ever achieved by a U.S. spacecraft en route to the ISS. They join Expedition 75 for a roughly six-month stay focused on human-health and microgravity research.

🇪🇸 SpaceX lanzó la misión Crew-13 de la NASA el 1 de octubre, llevando a cuatro astronautas a la Estación Espacial Internacional a bordo de un Falcon 9 y una Crew Dragon desde Cabo Cañaveral, Florida. La tripulación —Jessica Watkins y Luke Delaney de la NASA, Joshua Kutryk de Canadá y Sergey Teteryatnikov de Rusia— acopló unas 7 horas y 50 minutos después del despegue, el tiempo de acoplamiento más rápido logrado por una nave estadounidense rumbo a la EEI. Se unen a la Expedición 75 para una estancia de unos seis meses dedicada a investigación de salud humana y microgravedad.

Sources: NASA, Space.com — Oct. 1, 2026.
